# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).

## Goal

Implement the herdr hydrator module (packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts): every 30s (and on worklist focus-resume) it fetches all in_progress work items, matches each against work-item IDs in active pane titles across all tabs of the current workspace, and demotes any item with no matching pane per the signal-based rule (AC3 of parent WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI). Pure decision functions + orchestration with injectable deps; fail-open at every boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. extractWorkItemIdsFromPaneTitles(panes) returns WL-[0-9A-Z]+ IDs found in pane labels.
2. isActivePaneMatch(itemId, panes) returns true iff the ID appears in a running pane's label in any tab of the current workspace; workspace filtering via herdr pane list --workspace <id> / HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID env var.
3. decideDemotion(workItem, blockers): stage in_review → {status: completed, stage: in_review}; active outbound blocker (target not completed/deleted, stage not in_review/done, per isDependencyActive in packages/shared/src/database.ts) → {status: blocked, stage: plan_complete (or best compatible)}; else → {status: open, stage: intake_complete}; stage always chosen per src/config.ts compatibility.
4. runHydrationOnce(deps): fetches wl list --status in_progress, fetches panes, computes demotions, applies each via wl update (status+stage); an item with a matching pane is never touched.
5. Fail-open: wl/pane CLI missing, non-zero exit, or unparseable output → skip the entire cycle with a log; the function never throws; no demotion happens on untrustworthy evidence.
6. All hydrator.test.ts tests pass; full project suite passes.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts — new module
- packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts — reuse runWl/extractJson/extractItems
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts — orchestration precedent
- src/commands/dep.ts + packages/shared/src/database.ts — dependency semantics (reference only)
- src/config.ts — status/stage compatibility (reference only)

## Minimal Implementation

1. Pure helpers: extractWorkItemIdsFromPaneTitles, isActivePaneMatch, decideDemotion (status, stage) pair.
2. runHydrationOnce(deps) with injectable {runWl, runPaneList, now, log}; fetch in_progress; fetch panes filtered to workspace; outbound-edge stage fetch per blocker candidate (wl dep list carries status only — fetch stage via wl show for each edge not completed/deleted).
3. Apply demotions; wrap whole cycle in try/catch that logs and returns without demoting.

## Dependencies

- Requires F1 (hydrator.test.ts — written first; suite must pass to close)
- Requires F0 (pane-title format amendment — ID must survive truncation)

# Intake Brief: help screen and improved help line (WL-0MTV97GV20088CS7)

## Problem statement

The Herdr work-item selection list footer advertises only a small, mixed-signal
subset of the available keyboard shortcuts — including the low-value
`d:downtime toggle` and the mouse-tracking hint `alt+m mouse on` — while offering
no discoverable reference for the full command set or for the meaning of the
icons rendered on each row. Users cannot discover what keys are available or
what the glyphs mean without reading the source.

## Users

Herdr producers and agents who navigate work items in the pane-based selection
list and rely on the footer and on-screen glyphs to operate the tool.

**User stories:**

- As a Herdr user, I want a single `?` shortcut that opens a help screen, so I
  can discover every available command without reading the source.
- As a Herdr user, I want the help screen to explain every icon shown in the
  list, so I can interpret the status, stage, priority, risk, effort, audit and
  agent glyphs at a glance.
- As a Herdr user, I want the footer help line to advertise the help screen
  rather than rarely-used toggles, so the most useful discovery path is always
  visible.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Footer help line updated** — In the selection list footer, the
   `d:downtime toggle` entry is no longer advertised and `?: Help` is shown
   instead. The `d` key binding itself remains functional (only its inline
   advertisement is removed).
2. **Mouse hint removed from footer** — The `alt+m mouse on` / `alt+m mouse off`
   footer hint is removed. The `Alt+m` mouse-tracking toggle itself remains
   functional and is documented in the help screen.
3. **Help screen opens on `?`** — Pressing `?` in the selection list opens a
   dedicated help screen (full-pane overlay). Pressing `?`, `Esc`, or `q`
   dismisses it and returns to the list with no state mutation (selection,
   filters, and navigation stack unchanged).
4. **Help screen lists all commands** — The help screen enumerates every
   registered shortcut available in the selection list, grouped by chord
   leader, showing the chord key(s), label and a short description. The list is
   derived from the live `ShortcutRegistry` so future shortcut additions appear
   automatically.
5. **Help screen identifies all icons** — The help screen includes an icon
   legend that identifies every glyph rendered in work-item rows (at minimum:
   status, stage, priority, epic, risk, effort, audit, producer-review, agent
   state and child-coverage icons), each with a short meaning.
6. **Graceful on small panes** — The help screen renders within the pane height
   without overflowing the `rows - 1` render budget (scroll or truncate when
   content exceeds the viewport; the dismiss keys remain discoverable).
7. **Tests** — New/updated tests verify: (a) the footer shows `?: Help` and no
   longer shows `d:downtime toggle` or `alt+m mouse on/off`; (b) the help
   screen renders the registered commands and the icon legend; (c) `?` toggles
   the help screen on and off without mutating list state.
8. **Documentation** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, `docs/TUI.md`, the icon legend in
   `docs/icons-design.md` (if the on-screen legend wording is authoritative) and
   any relevant README entries.
9. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Must not break existing chord handling: `?` must not conflict with any
  registered shortcut chord or navigation key.
- Backward compatibility: all existing shortcut key bindings (including `d` and
  `Alt+m`) continue to function unchanged; only their footer advertisement
  changes.
- The help screen is display-only/read-only — it must not dispatch commands, spawn
  panes, or mutate the worklog.
- Icon legend content must be derived from the single source of truth
  (`@worklog/shared/icons`) rather than a hand-maintained duplicate list, so it
  cannot drift.
- Must respect the existing `showHelpText` gate (when help text is disabled, the
  help screen and its footer hint are not offered).

## Existing state

- **Footer hint assembly** — `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` composes the
  footer from `formatFooterShortcutHints()` (single-key entries render as
  `key:label`) plus an explicit mouse-tracking hint appended at render time
  (`dynamicHints` around the "Mouse-tracking toggle hint
  (WL-0MT0AP2LR000JFWN)" block). The `d` entry comes from
  `src/shortcuts.json` (`chord: ["d"]`, `label: "downtime toggle"`).
- **View modes** — `ViewMode = 'list' | 'detail' | 'filter' | 'form'`
  (`worklist.ts`). `renderWorklist()` branches on mode; `filter` mode shows a
  simple full-pane prompt — the closest existing precedent for a full-pane help
  overlay.
- **Key handling** — `keyToAction()` maps navigation keys; single-key shortcut
  resolution and chord handling happen in the main key loop. No `?` handling
  exists today.
- **Icons** — all row glyphs come from `@worklog/shared/icons`
  (`statusIcon`, `stageIcon`, `priorityIcon`, `epicIcon`, `riskIcon`,
  `effortIcon`, `auditIcon`, `needsProducerReviewIcon`, `agentStatusIcon`,
  `getIconPrefixParts`/`isCoveredByParent`). `docs/icons-design.md` documents the
  icon set and accessible labels.
- **Shortcut registry** — `ShortcutRegistry.getChordEntries()` /
  `getEntriesForStage()` expose all valid entries with `chord`, `label` and
  `description`, gated by code-freeze and issue-type.

## Desired change

1. **Footer (`formatFooterShortcutHints` / render-time composition):**
   - Exclude the `d:downtime toggle` single-key entry from the footer hint (or
     suppress its advertisement while keeping the binding).
   - Prepend/insert a literal `?: Help` hint.
   - Remove the `alt+m mouse on/off` suffix block.

2. **New help mode:** add `'help'` to `ViewMode`; render a full-pane help
   overlay in `renderWorklist()` with two sections — **Commands** (grouped by
   leader, `chord → label — description`) and **Icons** (glyph → meaning) —
   respecting the pane height budget.

3. **Key binding:** in list mode, `?` toggles the help mode on; inside help
   mode, `?`, `Esc` and `q` return to the previous mode (record the
   pre-help mode, mirroring the existing `preFormMode` pattern).

4. **Tests:** extend `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (and/or a focused
   `worklist-help.test.ts`) for the footer and help-screen behaviour.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `ViewMode`, `formatFooterShortcutHints()`,
  footer composition (mouse-hint block), `renderWorklist()` help overlay, key
  handling (`?`), help-content builder.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — `ShortcutRegistry` used to enumerate
  commands for the help screen (read-only; no signature change expected).
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — icon definitions used to build the legend
  (read-only; source of truth).
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — shortcut definitions; no new entry
  required if `?` is a reserved key, but a `?` entry may be added for
  discoverability.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (and/or new
  `packages/herdr/src/worklist-help.test.ts`) — footer and help-screen tests.
- `docs/TUI.md` — document the `?` help screen and updated footer.
- `docs/icons-design.md` — icon legend reference (update if wording is
  authoritative).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — shortcut/help summary if present.

## Related work

- **WL-0MQDR5HZC006JWOK** — "Show available shortcut keys in browse list help
  text" (completed). Introduced the dynamic shortcut hint line this work
  extends.
- **WL-0MRMG8P2X004V6YC** — "help line for chord commands too verbose"
  (completed). Collapsed/trimmed chord hints in the same footer.
- **WL-0MQDUOK9K002QHJU** — "Stage-based shortcut condition filters" (completed).
  Added stage-aware shortcut filtering used when enumerating help entries.
- **WL-0MT0AP2LR000JFWN** — mouse-tracking toggle (`Alt+m`) whose footer hint
  this work removes.
- **WL-0MSZ4NSOE007AQEF** — `/downtime toggle` command backing the `d` shortcut.
- **WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ** — "Herdr worklist: mouse and touch support in the
  selection list" (completed). Directly related: owns the mouse-tracking
  behaviour whose `Alt+m` footer hint this work removes.
- **WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94** — heading/display-row model used by the renderer.
- **WL-0MTV979LK005YB1B** — footer wrap guard (relevant to keeping the help
  overlay within the render budget).

None of these are duplicates or blockers — they provide historical context for
the footer, chord and renderer subsystems.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MTD0IVNN003WCOB** – Warn in wl export/import --help that export dumps the whole DB and import REPLACEs it (completed)
- **WL-0MUN4ARHA001SN40** – Research classic enemies from the arcade games of old (open)
- **WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ** – Herdr worklist: mouse and touch support in the selection list (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: add, alt, commands, downtime, help (+13 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: add, alt, commands, downtime, help (+13 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: add, alt, downtime, help, icons (+10 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — `d` binding retained:** "replace `d:downtime toggle` with
  `?: Help`" is interpreted as replacing the footer *advertisement* only; the
  `d` key continues to toggle downtime and is documented in the help screen.
- **Assumption — `Alt+m` retained:** the mouse-tracking toggle remains
  functional; only its footer advertisement is removed (documented in the help
  screen).
- **Assumption — list view scope:** the help screen is offered in the selection
  list. Detail-view command help is out of scope unless trivially reachable.
- **Risk — key conflict:** `?` must not collide with a registered chord or
  navigation key; verify against `shortcuts.json` and `keyToAction()`.
- **Risk — icon-legend drift:** hard-coding the legend duplicates the icon
  source of truth. Mitigate by deriving rows from `@worklog/shared/icons` where
  practical, or add a test asserting every legend glyph matches the exported
  icon.
- **Scope-creep risk:** a full command *reference* (rendering help text for
  detail/form modes) is out of scope; record such follow-ups as linked work
  items rather than expanding this one.
- **Small-pane risk:** the combined commands + icons content can exceed short
  panes; require truncation/scroll so the footer stays one row and the render
  invariant holds.
- **Performance risk:** negligible — help content is computed only when the
  help screen is opened.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were asked — the work-item description and code analysis
provided sufficient detail. Assumptions above were applied where the seed
context was ambiguous and are recorded for producer review.

When the audit runner runs child audits in separate-process mode (`--no-child-in-main-slot`), each child Phase-1 AC screen spawned a pi subprocess whose output could not be parsed: 'Warning: Unparseable Pi output for AC evaluation — falling back to partial verdict'. All child ACs were persisted as partial ('Ready to close: No'), which then reverted the in_review children to open/plan_complete and (via dependency reconciliation) to blocked — cascading a parent audit to 'Ready to close: No' even though the parent's own ACs were all met.

The default in-main-slot mode avoids this (child screens are performed by the invoking session), which is how the parent was ultimately verified green. Suggest: make separate-process child screening resilient to the local-proxy output format (or detect the unparseable case and retry/escalate instead of persisting partial), so the mode is usable in this environment.

# Dispatcher workspace has a useless blank pane

## Scope update (2026-09-29)

The dispatch placement architecture has changed since intake: automated panes
are no longer placed in per-prefix tabs inside a single `Dispatcher`
workspace — they are placed in **item-ID tabs inside each project's own
workspace** (`resolveProjectWorkspace` + `getItemTabAnchor`,
WL-0MU321YK70035AYT). The `Dispatcher` workspace is now only a fallback (for
unresolvable roots and scheduled prompts).

Both provisioning paths create a tab with herdr's automatically-provisioned
**root pane** (an empty bash pane):

- **Dispatcher fallback** (`getDispatcherAnchor`): the workspace's initial
  root pane is adopted into a `Downtime` tab via
  `herdr pane move <id> --new-tab --tab-label Downtime --no-focus`
  (implemented in 8a7180a8).
- **Project workspace item tabs** (`getItemTabAnchor`): the tab created via
  `herdr tab create --workspace <id> --label <itemId> --no-focus` also carries
  an empty bash pane (its root pane). This is the remaining "useless pane"
  the manual review flagged, and is fixed here.

## Problem statement

When a herdr tab is provisioned (`herdr workspace create` for the `Dispatcher`
fallback, or `herdr tab create` for a project-workspace item tab), herdr
automatically provisions a root pane. For the `Dispatcher` workspace the root
pane was persisted as the legacy `downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` but never
adopted by any tab. For project-workspace item tabs the root pane was only
ever used as the split anchor for the first dispatch and then left behind —
leaving each item tab with an empty bash pane alongside the productive
`Downtime triggered …` dispatch pane.

## Users

- **Downtime dispatcher operator** (Map/agent): the project workspace/Dispatcher
  workspace should display only productive panes, not an empty bash pane that
  adds clutter.
- **herdr interactive user**: a neutral workspace should show relevant panes only.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **No blank root pane on first provision**:
   - Dispatcher fallback: the workspace's initial root pane is adopted (as a
     tab) rather than left blank.
   - Project-workspace item tab: the tab's initial root pane (empty bash pane)
     is closed after the first dispatch pane spawns, so the tab contains only
     the productive dispatch pane.
2. **Idempotent re-provisioning**: on subsequent dispatch cycles the existing
   workspace/tab is reused without creating additional blank panes; closing
   the item-tab root pane never triggers a re-provision loop, and the
   Dispatcher fallback anchor is never closed (closing it would re-provision a
   blank pane).
3. **Item tab anchors preserved**: each work-item tab continues to function
   correctly — the first dispatch anchors to the tab root pane; later
   dispatches reuse the surviving dispatch pane as the split anchor; the tab
   is reused (never duplicated).
4. **No regression to dispatch**: all downtime dispatch flows continue to
   route to the correct project CWD and pane placement;
   `send-to-pi.sh --anchor <pane-id>` works with the new layout.
5. **Test coverage**: existing `packages/herdr` test suite passes; new/updated
   tests cover the provision and root-pane-cleanup paths.

## Constraints

- The fix must be within `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` and related files — do not modify
  `send-to-pi.sh` or `grid.py`.
- Must respect `--no-focus` semantics (never steal focus from the user's
  interactive workspace).
- Must be concurrency-safe (coordination lock pattern already established).
- Must not break the backward-compatible anchor file format
  (`downtime-dispatch-anchor.json`).
- Root-pane cleanup must be fail-safe: never close a live dispatch pane; when
  liveness cannot be positively confirmed, leave the anchor open.

## Existing state

- `getDispatcherAnchor()` creates the workspace and stores the root pane ID in
  `downtime-dispatch-anchor.json`; the root pane is adopted into a `Downtime`
  tab.
- `getItemTabAnchor()` finds-or-creates a tab labelled with the exact work-item
  id in the resolved project workspace; the tab's root pane (empty bash pane)
  was previously left behind after dispatch.
- Code: `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (`dispatchDowntimeWork`).

## Desired change

- **Dispatcher fallback**: after `createWorkspace` returns
  `{ workspaceId, paneId }`, adopt the root pane into a `Downtime` tab via
  `herdr pane move <rootPaneId> --new-tab --tab-label Downtime --no-focus` and
  persist the (unchanged) pane id. Implemented in 8a7180a8.

- `herdr workspace create` / `herdr tab create` have no option to suppress the
  root pane — it is always created.
- `herdr pane move <pane-id> --tab <tab-id> --no-focus` can move a pane into an

- `herdr pane move <pane-id> --new-tab --tab-label <label> --no-focus` can move

  fallback anchor (would trigger a re-provision loop), but IS used for a
  project-workspace item tab's root pane after the first dispatch.

- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` — `getDispatcherAnchor()`,
  `getItemTabAnchor()`, `createWorkspace`/`movePaneToNewTab` in deps
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — dispatch path
  (`dispatchDowntimeWork`) root-pane cleanup
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — wiring of dispatcher anchor resolver
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` and
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — unit tests

## Related work

- **WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG** (completed): Downtime dispatch panes all spawn in the
  leader's workspace regardless of project (C0: anchor-by-ID into dedicated
  Dispatcher workspace) — parent of the anchor provisioning work.
- **WL-0MTR2CD4X006XI7U** (completed): Implement dispatcher anchor provisioning

- **WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC** (open): Downtime dispatcher: per-project tabs in
  Dispatcher workspace — superseded by item-ID tabs in the project workspace
  (WL-0MU321YK70035AYT).

## Headline

herdr tabs are always provisioned with an initial root pane — an empty bash
pane. The `Dispatcher` fallback workspace adopts its root pane into a
`Downtime` tab; project-workspace item tabs previously left their root pane
behind next to the productive dispatch pane. This item closes that remaining
empty-pane gap.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: `herdr workspace create` / `herdr tab create` always create a
  root pane. **Confirmed** — no CLI option to suppress.
- **Assumption**: The root pane can be adopted by a tab (fallback) and closed
  after the first dispatch (item tabs). **Confirmed** — `herdr pane move
  --new-tab` and `herdr pane close`.
- **Risk**: Closing the Dispatcher fallback anchor would break dispatch and
  trigger a re-provision loop. **Avoided** — the fallback anchor is never
  closed; only project-workspace item-tab root panes are.
- **Risk**: Closing a live dispatch pane would kill a running agent. **Avoided**

  confirms it is not a downtime dispatch pane.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What does 'reused' mean — adopt the root pane as a tab, close it, or
  something else?" — Answer: adopt it into a tab for the Dispatcher fallback;
  close it after the first dispatch for project-workspace item tabs.

# Intake Brief: Review Queue depth notification is incorrect (AH-0MUDYTQ55002NUSJ)

## Headline

When the herdr worklist review queue is deep, the footer banner currently always
says "— audits will drain it". It must instead say "— focus on audits" while any
review item still lacks a current audit, and "Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')" once
every review item is audited.

## Problem statement

The herdr worklist shows a review-queue-depth banner when the root-only
`completed/in_review` count reaches `browseItemCount`. Today the banner copy is
fixed ("… — audits will drain it"), so it gives the same instruction whether
audits are still outstanding or the queue is fully audited and ready to ship.
The copy should reflect the actual audit state so the producer knows whether to
keep running audits or to ship.

## Users

- **Producer / sprint lead** — reads the banner to decide the next action.
  - *User story:* As a producer, when the review queue is deep and some items
    still need auditing, I want the banner to say "focus on audits" so I know
    audits are the drain. When every item in the queue has a current audit, I
    want the banner to say "Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')" so I know I can ship.
- **Downtime dispatcher / operator** — must be unaffected: the banner is
  display-only and never gates dispatch (WL-0MTTSWC1X005P4VD).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the review queue is deep (root-only `completed/in_review` count ≥
   `browseItemCount`) **and** at least one root-level `in_review` item has an
   outstanding audit, the footer banner text reads exactly:
   `Review queue deep (<completed> of <browseItemCount> completed/in_review) — focus on audits`.
2. When the review queue is deep **and** no root-level `in_review` item has an
   outstanding audit, the footer banner text reads exactly:
   `Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')`.
3. "Outstanding audit" is determined by the existing audit-freshness semantics
   (`isAuditFresh` / `inReviewBucket`): an `in_review` item with no stored
   `auditedAt`, or whose stored audit is not current, counts as outstanding. A
   fresh, passed audit does not.
4. The banner remains display-only: it never disables downtime dispatch, never
   writes/clears `.herdr-downtime-disabled`, and does not change code-freeze
   banner behaviour or the `showHelpText` gate.
5. Automated tests assert the exact rendered banner text for both variants and
   for the boundaries (deep+outstanding → deep+none; deep → shallow), using the
   existing worklist render test seams.
6. All related documentation/code comments describing the banner are updated to
   the new copy and the outstanding-audit condition.

## Constraints

- **Source repository:** the banner is implemented in the **ContextHub** repo
  (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`), not in `AI_Hell`. This work item is tracked
  in the `AI_Hell` worklog (consistent with existing tooling work items such as
  AH-0MUDYHPPC008F7PV); implementation must target the ContextHub source tree.
- `browseItemCount` default 20, re-read live from settings (no restart).
- Root-only counting via `wl list --status completed --stage in_review
  --root-only --json` (same query as `fetchCompletedItemCount`).
- No new persistence mechanism; reuse existing fetch helpers where possible.
- Display-only; must not reintroduce the sprint-complete auto-disable
  (WL-0MTTSWC1X005P4VD RCA root cause A).
- Keep the change minimal: banner copy + the state needed to choose it.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` renders the banner in the footer branch
  (~3596–3617): `const bannerText = \`Review queue deep${countDisplay} — audits will drain it\`;`
  where `countDisplay` = ` (<completed> of <browseItemCount> completed/in_review)`.
- `refreshSprintState()` (~4531–4546) calls `fetchCompletedItemCount()`
  (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` ~684) and sets
  `sprintComplete = count >= liveBrowseCount`. Only a count is retained —
  per-item audit state is not currently available to the banner.
- `fetchCompletedItemCount()` runs `wl list --status completed --stage in_review
  --root-only --json` and returns the item count. `wl list --json` items expose
  `stage`, `status`, `auditedAt`, `auditResult`, `fingerprint`, `updatedAt`
  (but not `currentFingerprint`).
- Audit freshness is centralised: `isAuditFresh(...)` in
  `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` (~306) and the audit-aware bucket predicate
  `inReviewBucket(...)` in `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` (~360–389). The
  audit-dispatch tier uses the same predicate.
- There are currently **no automated tests** covering the banner text or
  `refreshSprintState` — this gap must be closed.

## Desired change

- Extend the banner-state refresh (or add a sibling helper) so it knows whether
  any root-level `in_review` item has an outstanding audit, in addition to the
  deep-queue boolean.
- Select the banner copy from that state:
  - outstanding audits → `Review queue deep (<n> of <browseItemCount> completed/in_review) — focus on audits`;
  - none outstanding → `Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')`.
- Add regression tests for both variants and the transition boundaries.

# Problem Statement

When using the developer cheat menu (Market Card Cheat) to replace a card in the market slot, the replacement card cannot be taken — the HUD shows "No affordable cards" and the card is not interactive.

# Users

- **Developer testers**: The cheat menu is a development/debugging tool used by the development team to test game scenarios quickly.

**User story**: As a developer tester, I want to add any card to the market via the cheat menu and immediately be able to take/buy that card, so that I can test game scenarios without being blocked by the card being unresponsive.

# Acceptance Criteria

1. **Cheat-placed cards are clickable**: After using the Market Card Cheat menu to replace a market slot with a card, clicking the card successfully moves it to the player's hand (no unresponsive card).
2. **Cheat card appears in affordability summary**: The card appears in the "Can buy:" HUD summary (e.g., "Can buy: 1 business") alongside other affordable cards of the same family.
3. **All card families work**: The fix works for all card families supported by the cheat menu (business, community-space, event, upgrade, staff).
4. **Existing cheat functionality preserved**: Filtering, searching, and replacing market cards continue to work as before.

# Constraints

- The fix must be surgical — only modify the `cheatReplaceMarketCard` function in `MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`.
- Cheat-generated cards already have unique IDs (`${templateId}--cheat-${nonce}`) and reset properties (level, incomeBonus, etc.) — `family` should follow the same explicit-set pattern.
- The fix must not affect production gameplay — the cheat menu is strictly a dev/debug tool.

# Existing state

- **Card templates** in `MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` are typed as `Omit<BusinessCard, 'family' | 'level' | 'incomeBonus' | 'synergyRangeBonus' | 'reputationBonus'>[]` — the `family` field is intentionally **omitted** from templates (it is inferred from the array source).
- **`cheatReplaceMarketCard`** in `MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` creates cheat cards by spreading the template:
  ```typescript
  const newCard: AnyCard = { ...(template as any), id: `${baseId}--cheat-${cheatNonce++}` } as AnyCard;
  ```
  The function explicitly resets `level`, `incomeBonus`, etc. for business/community-space cards, but **does not explicitly set `family`** — leaving it as `undefined`.
- **Market rendering** in `MainStreetRendererMarket.ts` determines click handlers by checking `card.family`:
  ```typescript
  if (card.family === 'business' || card.family === 'community-space') {
      s.onBusinessCardClick(card as BusinessCard);
  } else if (card.family === 'upgrade') { ... }
  ```
  When `card.family` is `undefined`, none of these conditions match, so the cheat card is not interactive.
- **Affordability check** in `MainStreetMarketUtils.ts` also filters by family:
  ```typescript
  c => (c.family === 'business' || c.family === 'community-space') && c.cost <= state.resourceBank.coins
  ```
  The `undefined` family fails this check, so the card is not shown as "affordable".

# Desired change

Explicitly set the `family` property on cheat-created cards to match the card's actual family, so that rendering and affordability checks work correctly.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — `cheatReplaceMarketCard` function, where the new card is created (fix location)
- `src/MainStreetMarketUtils.ts` — `getAffordableBusinessCards`, `getAffordableUpgradeCards` (affordability checks that depend on `family`)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts` — `refreshMarket` (rendering that routes click handlers by `family`)
- `src/debug/MarketCardCheatOverlay.ts` — `MarketCardCheatOverlay` (invokes the cheat function, already passes correct `family`)

# Related work

- **WL-0MUH5HU580064VMR** — "Show which cards are in the current deck in the market cards cheat" (related cheat menu feature, separate work item)

# Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption**: The root cause is the missing `family` field. Verified by code analysis — templates omit `family` and the cheat spread does not set it.
- **Risk**: Minimal scope creep — the fix is a single property assignment in the cheat function.
- **Risk**: If other card properties are also missing from cheat cards (beyond what is already explicitly reset), they may surface later during testing.
- **Risk**: None — no production gameplay impact (cheat menu is dev-only).

# Polish & Handoff

**Headline**: Cheat menu market replacements create cards without a `family` field, making them unclickable and invisible to affordability checks. Fix: explicitly set `family` in `cheatReplaceMarketCard`.

# Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions needed — the root cause was identified through code analysis. The bug is reproducible from the described steps:

1. Open settings → open market card cheat menu
2. Select any card type (e.g., "Pawn Shop")
3. Replace a market slot
4. Close settings
5. The replaced card is not clickable and the HUD shows "No affordable cards"

# Audit remaining mutating commands for the store-lock lost-update gap

## Problem statement

`wl sync` holds the per-store advisory file lock (`withFileLock` /
`getLockPathForJsonl`) for its whole fetch → merge → write-back → push
operation, but only a subset of mutating commands acquire that same lock around
their read-modify-write. The earlier fix (WL-0MUV2U9QF002S9J1) locked exactly
`wl update`, `wl comment add`, and `wl audit-set`. Every other DB-writing
command still performs an unlocked read-modify-write, so a `wl sync` that
overlaps one can be clobbered by the sync's stale snapshot — silently reverting
the mutation and, where applicable, dropping the accompanying comment. The gap
is already proven in production for `wl close` (WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ: 3 of 53
release closes lost with a success exit code).

## Users

- **Agents / producers running parallel sessions** on a shared store.
  - *As an agent that closes, deletes, re-parents, or dependency-edits an item,
    I want my mutation to survive a concurrent `wl sync` so finished work is not
    silently reverted.*
  - *As a release operator, I want `wl close` to be durable so a release does
    not leave items stranded in `in_review`.*
- **Worklog tool maintainers** responsible for `sync`, `file-lock`, and the
  mutating commands.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every `wl` subcommand that writes to the store is enumerated in an audit
   table on this work item, each row classifying the command as already holding
   the store mutation lock or not, and naming the unlocked ones.
2. Every unlocked mutating command's read-modify-write is wrapped in
   `withStoreMutationLock` (or the equivalent `withFileLock` +
   `getLockPathForJsonl` pair), including side-effect paths — `wl close --force`
   (recursive descendants + audit waivers), `wl delete` (the soft delete and its
   own auto-sync), `wl dep add` / `wl dep rm`, `wl re-sort`, `wl create`,
   `wl reviewed`, `wl audit-waive` / `wl audit-unwaive`, `wl interview`, and
   `wl github import`.
3. A concurrency regression test proves, for each command class, that a mutation
   landing during a concurrent `wl sync` read-modify-write survives (item state
   and any comment intact), reusing the deterministic parked-`git fetch` harness
   in `tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts`.
4. No regression: existing sync/sync serialisation, file-lock, and
   mutating-command tests pass; commands already correctly locked (`wl import`,
   `wl github push`, `wl sync`) are not double-locked in a way that deadlocks an
   internally-triggered auto-sync.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant docs-site entries (specifically the
   concurrency section of `docs/design/incremental-sync.md` and the locking
   section of `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`).
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing lock: `withStoreMutationLock(dataPath, fn)` in
  `src/mutation-lock.ts`. Do not introduce a second locking mechanism.
- `withFileLock` is reentrant per process, so a mutation that internally
  triggers `wl sync` (e.g. `wl delete`'s auto-sync) must not deadlock.
- Preserve all existing command semantics and output shapes; this is a
  durability fix, not a behaviour change.
- Destructive whole-store commands (`wl import`, `wl init`, `wl migrate`,
  `wl doctor migrate`) replace the store rather than mutate a record; they must
  hold the lock, but a lost-update *merge* regression test is not meaningful for
  them.
- Do not edit `.pi/`, `skill/`, or agent-infrastructure directories.

DB-writing command is accounted for. Commands verified as already locked:
`wl update`, `wl comment add`, `wl audit-set`, `wl import`, `wl github push`,

2. Wrap each unlocked command's full read-modify-write — including recursive

  named in the seed description (`close`, `dep`, `re-sort`, `github import/push`).
  The seed's acceptance says "enumerate every DB-writing command", so `create`,

  long recursive loops could stall other writers. Mitigation: keep the lock
  scoped to the local read-modify-write; confirm network calls stay outside or
  are bounded, as the existing `github push` path already does.

  chosen approach is the shared file lock.

# Cap the recovery retry-loop backoff at 10 minutes for all retry-path failures

Discovered from: WL-0MU56ZSSB0054D8W

## Problem statement

The recovery retry loop (`triggerInvisibleContinue` in `register-recovery.ts`)
currently caps every backoff interval at `DEFAULT_BACKOFF_CONFIG.maxDelayMs =
60000` (60s) in `retry-logic.ts`. For long-lived outages — for example the
llm-proxy provider quiet-hours window ("scheduled time window") that can last
hours — the loop keeps retrying roughly once a minute indefinitely. That is
wasteful (constant churn against the proxy and the agent) and does not reflect
that the outage is long. Raise the ceiling to **10 minutes (600000 ms)** so the
backoff can settle at up to one attempt per 10 minutes for **every** failure
that takes this route.

**User story:** As an operator/unattended agent, when a retryable outage lasts
longer than a few minutes, I want the recovery loop to keep retrying
automatically but with a backoff ceiling of 10 minutes, so retries do not
hammer the provider at a fixed 60s cadence for hours.

## Current state

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-logic.ts`:
  `DEFAULT_BACKOFF_CONFIG = { baseDelayMs: 2000, maxDelayMs: 60000,
  multiplier: 2, serverHintJitterRatio: 0.25 }`.
- `register-recovery.ts` (`triggerInvisibleContinue`) calls
  `resolveRetryDelay(attempt, lastErrorMessageFromAgentState(),
  DEFAULT_BACKOFF_CONFIG, Math.random, _lastServerRetryHintMs)` — so this single
  config governs **all** retryable-path failures: SERVER_ERROR, TIMEOUT, and
  the shared loop used by CONTEXT_LENGTH and COMPACTION_GATE recovery.
- `error-patterns.ts` `DEFAULT_RECOVERY_CONFIG.<category>.maxDelayMs` mirrors
  60000 for `serverError` and `timeout`; these are the settings surface, not the
  loop's actual cap.
- `calculateDelay()` caps both the local exponential and the server-hint
  (`Retry-After`) derived delay at `maxDelayMs`.
- Tests that will need updating: `retry-after-header.test.ts` (~line 118 asserts
  a 90_000 hint is clamped to the 60s default), `retry-after.test.ts`,
  `retry-loop.test.ts`, `settings.test.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `DEFAULT_BACKOFF_CONFIG.maxDelayMs` is `600000` (10 minutes); the constant
      is documented as the retry-loop ceiling.
- [ ] The shared retry loop reaches a 600000ms cap for high attempt numbers
      (e.g. attempt 10) across all categories that route through
      `triggerInvisibleContinue` — asserted via `calculateDelay` /
      `resolveRetryDelay`.
- [ ] A server `Retry-After` hint between 60s and 10m is honoured up to the
      600000ms cap (no longer clamped to 60000); a hint above 10m is clamped to
      600000.
- [ ] `DEFAULT_RECOVERY_CONFIG.<category>.maxDelayMs` values are made consistent
      with the new ceiling where they mirror it (`serverError`, `timeout`), or a
      comment explains why they differ.
- [ ] No regression: existing retry-after/retry-loop/retry-command/recovery
      tests pass with the updated expectations.
- [ ] Documentation/comments updated (`retry-logic.ts` and any related docs)
      describing the 10-minute ceiling.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Behaviour change only to the backoff ceiling; do **not** change base delay
  (2000ms), multiplier (2), or jitter.
- Keep the loop's single-layer design; no new dependencies.
- Closely related to `WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM` ("honour long server Retry-After
  hints, do not clamp to 60s"). Raising the cap to 10m partially addresses that;
  this item must state the interaction and not duplicate it. A hint longer than
  10m remains clamped by design (10m is the requested ceiling).
- Respect the user-abort (ESC) and session-switch guards — unchanged.

## Key files (predicted)

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-logic.ts` — raise
  `DEFAULT_BACKOFF_CONFIG.maxDelayMs`; update docs/comments.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts` — align
  per-category `maxDelayMs` (or document the intentional difference).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-after-header.test.ts`,
  `retry-after.test.ts`, `retry-loop.test.ts`, `settings.test.ts` — update/add
  cap assertions.

## Related work

- `WL-0MU56ZSSB0054D8W` (discovered-from) — classified the proxy scheduled-window
  503 as SERVER_ERROR; that retry path is the motivating case.
- `WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM` — honour long server Retry-After hints (do not clamp to
  60s); adjacent, overlapping on the clamp behaviour.
- `WL-0MUQO8AEE003G1Z2`, `WL-0MT656GDS0052FTK` — earlier work routing more errors
  into this retry path.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** 10 minutes is an acceptable maximum wait (operators accept up
  to 10m between automatic attempts in exchange for far less churn).
- **Risk:** raising the cap delays recovery for outages that resolve shortly
  after a long backoff; mitigated because the exponential ramp only reaches 10m
  after several attempts (2s, 4s, 8s, ... 10m).
- **Risk:** test expectations for the 60s clamp are updated in behaviour, not
  silently weakened.
data.title: Cap recovery retry-loop backoff at 10m for all retry-path failures

# Prevent tests posting a real Discord release notification (Release v9.9.9)

## Problem statement

Running the release test harness posts a real notification to the configured
Discord webhook, titled `Release v9.9.9`. The side effect is harmless (no data
loss, no production impact) but noisy: the message lands in a real release
channel on every test run, and tests must never perform real outbound
notifications.

## Users

- **Developer / operator running the full test suite** — should not see
  unexpected Discord noise when testing.
  - *As a developer, when I run the release tests, no message should be posted
    to the real Discord release channel.*
- **CI operator** — test runs must be deterministic and side-effect free.
  - *As a CI operator, a test run must not depend on, or mutate, any external
    service.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No real notification.** Running the identified release test harness
   produces **no outbound HTTP request to any real Discord webhook**. Verified
   by a test that fails if the real webhook would be resolved/called during the
   harness (or by asserting the notifier is stubbed and the global-config
   fallback is unreachable in the harness).
2. **Coverage retained.** The Step 8.5 notification wiring keeps test coverage
   through a mocked/stubbed notifier (the existing
   `test-run-release-discord-notify.mjs` pattern), so silencing the real send
   does not drop coverage.
3. **Regression guard.** The release integration harness cannot accidentally
   reach the real `discord-notify.js`/global webhook again — the harness injects
   a stub notifier (or an isolated global-config path/HOME), and a test pins
   this so a future copy of the real module cannot re-introduce the side effect.
4. **Testing/validation.** At least one test asserts the "no real Discord
   request" property described in AC1; the full project test suite is exercised
   locally to confirm no external notification is emitted.
5. **Docs updated.** The test-isolation rule ("tests never perform real release
   notifications") is documented in the relevant test/README or ship-skill
   reference; all related documentation, code comments, README, and any
   relevant wiki/docs-site entries are updated.
6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Production behaviour unchanged.** Real releases must still post the Discord
  notification; only test runs must be silenced.
- **Fix at the harness boundary.** Prefer stubbing the notifier module or
  isolating the global config inside the test harness, consistent with the
  existing `test-run-release-discord-notify.mjs` pattern, over changing
  production notification logic.
- **No secrets, no global mutation.** Do not commit any webhook token and do
  not mutate the operator's real `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml`; isolate per test
  process if the config path is redirected.
- **Minimal, targeted change.** Do not remove or weaken unrelated release tests.

## Existing state

- `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` resolves the webhook via
  `resolveDiscordWebhookUrl()` in three layers: project
  `.worklog/config.private.yaml` → project `.worklog/config.yaml` → global
  `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml`. The first hit wins; if none is set the
  notification is skipped.
- `run-release.js` calls `sendReleaseNotification({ version, prUrl, projectRoot })`
  at Step 8.5. The version comes from `git describe --tags --abbrev=0`.
- The offender is `tests/unit/test-run-release-merge-guard.mjs` (shared ship
  skill test suite): it copies the **real** `discord-notify.js` into a temp
  skill layout and runs the **real** `run-release.js` with mocked `git`/`wl`/`gh`
  binaries. The mocked `git describe` returns `v9.9.9`, and the temp project
  root has no `.worklog/` config — so webhook resolution falls back to the
  operator's global `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml` and a real embed titled
  `Release v9.9.9` is POSTed. The process env (including `HOME`) is inherited,
  which is why the global fallback is reachable.
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-discord-notify.mjs` already replaces
  `discord-notify.js` with a recording stub and therefore does **not** send —
  this is the pattern to reuse.
- The ship skill's own `skill/ship/tests/test_discord_notify.mjs` injects
  `fetchFn` for every `sendReleaseNotification` call, so it does not send.

## Desired change

1. **Remove the offending test code** that causes the real Discord
   notification in the release integration harness: in
   `tests/unit/test-run-release-merge-guard.mjs`, stop copying/executing the
   real `discord-notify.js` (remove that part of the test) so the test no
   longer performs a real notification.
2. Keep the harness's actual purpose intact — the Step 8 merge-verification
   guard and the work-item close behaviour must still be covered and green.
3. Add a regression-guard assertion that the harness cannot reach the real
   notifier / global webhook, if a simple guard is warranted.
4. Keep (or rely on the existing `test-run-release-discord-notify.mjs`)
   coverage that Step 8.5 is invoked with the resolved `projectRoot`, version,
   and PR URL.
5. Document the "tests never post real release notifications" rule.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/unit/test-run-release-merge-guard.mjs` — The offender: copies the real
  `discord-notify.js` and inherits `HOME`; needs a stubbed notifier (or an
  isolated global-config path) so Step 8.5 cannot send.
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-discord-notify.mjs` — Reference pattern: already
  substitutes a mock notifier that records arguments; reuse this harness shape.
- `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` — Optional test-only guard (e.g. a
  `DISABLE_DISCORD_NOTIFY`/test-env short-circuit) **only** if harness-level
  stubbing is insufficient; production behaviour must be unchanged.
- `skill/ship/tests/test_discord_notify.mjs` — Confirm coverage of
  `sendReleaseNotification` remains intact after the change.
- `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` and/or the test suite README —
  Document the test-isolation rule.

## Related work

- **WL-0MN1X7DIT0UVXTC8** — Remove TUI browser-opening test (completed). Same
  class of defect: a test performing a real external side effect. Its approach
  (mock the boundary or add a test-only guard; do not change production
  behaviour) is the precedent to follow.
- **WL-0MUWEPN6X0044R43** — Consume the project CTA in release reports (open).
  Also touches the ship-skill Discord release notification composition.
- **WL-0MURIXAHY0031JIJ** — Send standup reports to discord using the same
  webhook as the ship skill (open). Shares the same webhook/config resolution;
  any test-isolation convention should be consistent across these items.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (target location).** The offending tests live in the shared ship
  skill test harness — currently provided by the agent-framework skill tree
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills/ship`, symlinked from the SorraAgents repo), not in this
  repository's own vitest suite. This repository does not currently contain a
  `skill/ship` tree. If the operator intends the fix to land in this repository
  instead, the harness must first be vendored here (separate work).
- **Risk (scope creep).** "Fixing" this by changing production
  `discord-notify.js` could weaken real release notifications. **Mitigation:**
  prefer harness-level stubbing; add a production guard only if strictly
  necessary, and keep it opt-in.
- **Risk (false safety).** Over-mocking could hide a real Step 8.5 wiring
  regression. **Mitigation:** retain the dedicated wiring test
  (`test-run-release-discord-notify.mjs`).
- **Risk (environment coupling).** Redirecting `HOME` could affect unrelated
  behaviour of the spawned `run-release.js`/`git`/`wl` mocks. **Mitigation:**
  inject an explicit `globalConfigPath` (or stub the notifier) rather than
  changing `HOME` wholesale.
- **Failure mode.** If the harness stubs the notifier but the assertion set is
  incomplete, a future test could re-copy the real module. **Mitigation:** AC3
  regression guard.
- **Scope control.** Wiring the resolved CTA into the notification is the
  separate open item WL-0MUWEPN6X0044R43 and is **not** in scope here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: **Which repository/test suite is the target of this fix?** The seed says
  "tests for ContextHub", but this repository's vitest suite does not send any
  Discord message; the only confirmed sender is the shared ship-skill
  integration test `tests/unit/test-run-release-merge-guard.mjs`, which copies
  the real `discord-notify.js` and executes `run-release.js` with an inherited
  `HOME`, falling back to the global `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml` webhook.
  Answer (operator, interactive): "Just remove that part of the test code." —
  remove the offending test code that triggers the real notification, rather
  than adding a guard/stub. Source: interactive reply.
  Note: the offending test lives in the shared ship-skill harness
  (`tests/unit/test-run-release-merge-guard.mjs`), which is not present in this
  repository; implementation must target that harness.
- Q: **Is the noisy message acceptable to leave until a later release, or must
  it be silenced now?** Answer (operator, seed intent): "This is harmless but
  noisy, remove it." — remove now. Source: interactive seed context.

packages/herdr/scripts/tests/test_run_in_pane.sh starts the --exec wrapper with HERDR_PANE_ID set, which runs 'sleep infinity' to keep the pane alive. The test kills the wrapper bash PID but not the grandchild 'sleep infinity', which is reparented to init and inherits the script's stdout. Any invocation piped to tail/head (e.g. 'bash test_run_in_pane.sh 2>&1 | tail -35') therefore never sees EOF and hangs indefinitely, even under 'timeout N' (timeout kills the direct child; the orphan keeps the pipe open). This caused multiple driven child sessions to hang during WL-0MUKZGEQ2007FECS. Suggested fix: kill the whole process group / reap the grandchild (e.g. run the background wrapper via setsid and kill the group, or track and kill the 'sleep infinity' PID), and/or send its output to a file rather than a pipe.
